result.method_note: Model response where it reacts, merit-order estimate elsewhere. Cost is price change × forecast demand × hours. This approximates market coupling. Extra Scottish wind beyond spare B6 boundary capacity is assumed curtailed and paid about £75/MWh (estimates); only the rest lowers the GB price.

body.note: Ghost wind is estimated from accepted bids on mapped Scottish wind units (an upper bound on constraint curtailment) and from weather-implied minus metered output (modelled, generic power curve). Constraint costs are NESO actuals, newest 10 days old. Boundary flows are NESO day-ahead forecasts.

Emission factors are standard estimates; consumption intensity is modelled. BE looks cleaner than it is: it generates at 342 g/kWh but consumes at 379 g/kWh once imports are counted, mostly from NL. FR looks cleaner than it is: it generates at 77 g/kWh but consumes at 92 g/kWh once imports are counted, mostly from BE.

body.note: Estimates. Boundary flows are NESO day-ahead forecasts, not metered flows, over a short window. The counterfactual changes one limit and prices the avoided volume at NESO's average thermal cost per MWh for that day; it ignores other boundaries that would then bind and the market response. The Scottish boundaries are nested (SSEN-S, SSE-SP and SSHARN also exceed their limits in the same window), so avoided cost and wind are upper bounds. Accepted wind bids include non-constraint actions, so avoided wind is an upper bound too.

body.note: Unit rates only: standing charges are the same however you use the energy. Agile rates are Octopus's published half-hourly prices; tonight's later hours use our GB day-ahead forecast through the Agile formula and are labelled forecast. The cap rate is Ofgem's for 1 October to 31 December 2026 (26.6p/kWh in London), so cap comparisons by month exist only for months inside that period and the annual cap figure assumes the whole year had been billed at that rate. No typical fixed tariff rate is verified, so a fixed comparison appears only if you supply fixed_p_kwh. Monthly savings take each day's best window against starting at 6 pm, scaled to the usage shown; months with under 20 days of prices are marked partial and left out of the range. Device usage marked assumption is ours.

body.note: Estimate for 1,000 H100 GPUs at 60% utilisation, PUE 1.5, 20% of work movable within the day. NVIDIA DGX H100: 10.2 kW max for 8 GPUs, whole system; power is taken as linear in utilisation, which understates idle draw. Default PUE is Uptime Institute's 2025 European average (1.50); utilisation and flexible share are our assumptions. Costs are wholesale energy at the trailing year's prices (modelled, not a quote): no network charges, levies, taxes or power-purchase terms. Carbon uses modelled consumption-based intensity; its cost prices the tonnes at the EU ETS allowance price and is already part of the power price, so do not add it to the energy cost. Moving flexible work to cheap hours can raise or lower carbon; both are shown.
